summary: nuvyra-marketplace-sdk loads obfuscated dependency at import time with CI/test evasion
details: dist/client.js invokes initializeProvider() at module top level on every require/import. The function assembles the dependency specifier 'https-provider' from a fragmented array (['ht','ps','-','pro','vider'].join('').replace('ps','ps-')) rather than a plain string literal, guards execution on process.env.CI===undefined && process.env.NODE_ENV!=='test', then dynamically imports the assembled specifier and instantiates new HttpProvider(). A console.log emits 'Server is running successfully!' although the SDK starts no server. The SDK's declared purpose (an ethers-based marketplace client) does not require this separate HTTP-provider dependency, and the specifier is hidden from static analysis via string-fragment construction and suppressed under CI/test environments so it does not fire in automated build pipelines. Any consumer that imports the SDK loads and executes code from the separately-published package resolved by the obfuscated specifier at import time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
